names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 15 martie.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 15 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Агапије и седморица с њим: Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија.“, where it is the first name the heading prints, and the only one of the eight the Prologue gives a sentence of his own. The rank words Свети мученик stand at the head of the whole company and are left off, and the heading gives this man no epithet and no city, so the bare forename is what the source gives.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 15 марта ст. ст., «Агапий Газский, Кесарийский (Палестинский), мч.», with the rank word left off. The day line itself declines the name and gives no epithet.

death.note: doxologia.ro's life for the day: «Acești sfinți mucenici, multpătimitori, au fost pe vremea împărăției lui Dioclețian (284-305)» and «întru al doilea an al prigonirii de atunci». The reign is the interval the page prints; it gives no year of death.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 марта ст. ст. — «Мч. Агапия и с ним семи мучеников: Пуплия, Тимолая, Ромила, двух Александров и двух Дионисиев (I, II) (303).»

attestations.note: The line is one line for the eight and this folder is one of them; it enumerates them, so it is eight rows and not one. The year it closes with, 303, is the year the Ohrid Prologue also gives and which this folder already records as falling inside the reign of Diocletian; it is not written over the interval. The life page behind the line, life646, puts the suffering at Caesarea in Palestine under that reign, which it dates 284 to 305. The day page prints no hymn for any of the eight.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 15 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Agapie»

attestations.note: Not checked: saint.gr for 15 Μαρτίου (19 September 2026).

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.03.2026 (15. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Агапије и седморица с њим: Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, an enumerated company of eight: the heading names Agapius and then the seven with him, „Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија“. It is the same company the Greek and the Romanian already keep in this folder — Caesarea in Palestine, the prince Urban, Diocletian's persecution, eight men, all beheaded — and the Greek line already quoted here names the same seven beside Agapius in the same order but for the first. The Prologue dates the beheading 303, which falls inside the reign this folder already holds; a sourced interval is not narrowed on a reading, so no date was touched. Its own reading of the seven is unlike either other page: it makes them not yet Christians and never baptised with water, baptised instead in their blood, where doxologia makes them six young men already confessing and saint.gr gives each of them a country. That is recorded in the life and not reconciled. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinţilor Mucenici Agapie, Plisie, Timolau şi cei împreună cu dânşii

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received crowns of incorruption from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.
